title: N.C.R.B., (M.H.A.) CRIME IN INDIA-1995 17.5.4 The above figures which include baggage seizures, demonstrate that there has been a fall in the smuggling of precious metals over the years since 1992. The quantity of gold smuggled has also fallen from 4946 kgs in 1991 to 1169 in 1995. Similar is the case with silver which recorded 197925 kgs in 1991 had dwindled to 678 kgs in 1995. 'Narcotic Drugs' arc, however, found to be in the priority list of smuggling in 1995 compared to the previous years. There has been a sharp increase of around 58 per cent (from 54.3 crores in 1994 to 85.7 crores in 1995) in the value of the 'Drugs' seized by the customs. Electronic goods also seem to be much sought after items for smuggling in 1995 because of perceived premium and the value of the seized articles accounting to Rs.63.3 crores compared to Rs.37.2 crores in 1994.
